elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Article III is untouched: "Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein," and customization work is a Derivative Work of the Platform Software; the insertion grants only a licence, not ownership, of the Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere; the operative insertion says only "Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence."

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Article III retained in full: Licensor owns all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology (Licensed Know-How plus Licensed Software) and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual ... licence to use, modify and sublicense ... any customization or development work performed for Licensee under this Section (the 'Deliverables')," and the Notwithstanding overrides Article XXI's automatic licence termination; the grant covers the Deliverables including Licensor IP within them.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Insertion reads "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence," notwithstanding Articles II, III, VI and XXI.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The insertion only limits Licensor's use ("Any licence or right of Licensor in data ... is limited to processing such data solely to provide the services"); no affirmative sentence stating Licensee retains all right, title and interest in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for it.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any licence or right of Licensor in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee is limited to processing such data solely to provide the services under this Agreement." No retained resale/independent-exploitation right in Licensee data appears in the cited text.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership language exists in the retained or inserted text; Article III vests sole ownership of Licensed Technology in Licensor, and the insertion creates only a licence, so the condition (delete joint ownership) does not arise.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Article III preserved unamended: Licensor owns all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology (defined as Licensed Know-How and Licensed Software) and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "Notwithstanding Articles II, III, VI and XXI, Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual ... licence ..."; the XXI override neutralises the automatic licence termination on expiry/termination.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Express "worldwide" in the inserted grant; no Field-of-Use or territory qualifier is applied to the Deliverables licence because the grant overrides Article II.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "licence to use, modify and sublicense for Licensee's business any customization or development work performed for Licensee under this Section"; the Notwithstanding Article II override displaces the II(g) no-modification-without-consent restriction as to Deliverables.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "use, modify and sublicense for Licensee's business"; the override of Articles II and VI displaces the II(c) sublicense/transfer prohibition as to the Deliverables.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Second inserted sentence covers every category — "data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee" — and confines Licensor to "processing such data solely to provide the services under this Agreement."

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single inserted grant supplies all four licence modifiers (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free), the use/modify and sublicense rights for Licensee's business, and the data-use limitation, while Article III leaves Licensor's ownership of its platform and know-how intact.

Preferred level is not reached: there is no Customer ownership of, or Vendor assignment of, the customization Deliverables, and no affirmative sentence that Licensee retains all rights in its data. To reach preferred the drafter would need an operative 'Licensor hereby assigns to Licensee all right, title and interest in the Deliverables' sentence plus a 'Licensee retains all right, title and interest in Licensee data' sentence.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion at the customization clause, no deletions, no survival tails, expense, indemnity or procedural extras. The Notwithstanding reference to Articles II, III, VI and XXI is not gratuitous boilerplate here — without it the retained II(c) sublicense ban, II(g) modification ban, Article III ownership/copy restriction and Article XXI automatic licence termination would each directly contradict the new grant and render the licence internally inconsistent.

Intent is preserved: the Field-of-Use limit, copy and notice restrictions, infringement-reporting duty and Article XXI return obligations continue to govern the Licensed Technology; the override is scoped to the Deliverables licence only, leaving no dangling term or undefined trigger ('Deliverables' is defined in the inserted text).

Minor residual to flag in the rationale only: Article XXI(b) still requires return of all Licensed Technology within five days, which sits awkwardly with a perpetual Deliverables licence if the Deliverables are treated as Derivative Works — a short carve-out ('other than the Deliverables licensed under Section VII(b)') would tidy this, but it is not required by any selected element.
